sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Speck, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 我是Gemma Speck，欢迎回到《20多岁的心理学》，在这个播客中，我们探讨20多岁时经历的最大变化、时刻和转型，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续剖析20多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Here is a story I hear a lot from listeners of the show.
sentences.zh: 这是我从听众那里经常听到的一个故事。

sentences.en: It is the story of someone being fresh out of college, fresh out of uni, getting their first job, starting a new job, being super optimistic and excited,
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于某人刚大学毕业，刚离开校园，找到第一份工作，开始新职业，充满乐观和兴奋的故事，

sentences.en: and they're excited for the security and for the paycheck and for the beginning of something new.
sentences.zh: 他们为这份工作的保障、薪水以及新事物的开始感到兴奋。

sentences.en: And then a few months in, they encounter someone who just wants to make their life miserable, whether that is a colleague, whether that is a boss, or they realize,
sentences.zh: 然后几个月后，他们遇到了一个只想让他们的生活变得痛苦的人，无论是同事还是老板，或者他们意识到，

sentences.en: hey, wait a second, this workplace literally feels like I'm back in high school.
sentences.zh: 嘿，等一下，这个工作场所感觉就像我回到了高中一样。

sentences.en: Why does this person have an issue with me?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个人对我意见这么大？

sentences.en: Why are these people sleeping together?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些人会搞在一起？

sentences.en: Why did I not get that promotion when I obviously work harder?
sentences.zh: 为什么我明明工作更努力，却没有得到晋升？

sentences.en: Why does this person just hate me?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个人就是讨厌我？

sentences.en: I hear a story about this probably every week, a story about office politics, about drama and backstabbing and affairs
sentences.zh: 我几乎每周都会听到这样的故事，关于办公室政治、关于勾心斗角、背地捅刀和绯闻，

sentences.en: and stuff that honestly nobody prepares us for in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 以及那些老实说在职场中没人教过我们如何应对的事情。

sentences.en: We spend so much time at work and office politics and situations like this do not get enough credit for how stressful they can be because we're often part of the stress
sentences.zh: 我们花在工作上的时间太多了，而办公室政治和类似的情况往往被低估了其压力程度，因为我们感到压力的一部分原因，

sentences.en: is we have zero idea what to do.
sentences.zh: 是我们完全不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: Especially in our 20s, we feel so helpless.
sentences.zh: 特别是在20多岁时，我们感到非常无助。

sentences.en: Our work begins to suffer.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作开始受到影响。

sentences.en: We feel pessimistic about work in general,
sentences.zh: 我们对工作整体感到悲观，

sentences.en: but how you go about managing these situations is going to shape your career deeply and possibly for the better.
sentences.zh: 但你如何处理这些情况将深刻地塑造你的职业生涯，而且可能是向好的方向发展。

sentences.en: And if you have the right tools, your approach to office politics could actually make you more successful.
sentences.zh: 如果你掌握了正确的工具，你处理办公室政治的方式实际上可以让你更成功。

sentences.en: Today, I want to give you a bit of that guide into the psychology that drives these hidden social mechanisms in the workplace and kind of the reminder that we need
sentences.zh: 今天，我想为你提供一点关于驱动职场这些隐藏社会机制的心理学指南，并提醒我们，

sentences.en: that all of this is just complex human behavior
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都只是复杂的行为，

sentences.en: boiled down into petty drama.
sentences.zh: 归根结底就是琐碎的闹剧。

sentences.en: Behind the scenes of all of this is secret motivations, emotions, human psychology that is influencing why people are the way we are or the way they are.
sentences.zh: 这一切幕后隐藏着秘密的动机、情绪和人类心理，它们影响着我们为什么会表现出现在的样子，或者他们为什么会那样做。

sentences.en: And when we understand that psychology, we understand that research and that science, we have a better emotional playbook for dealing with this
sentences.zh: 当我们理解了这些心理学、研究和科学，我们就有了更好的情感剧本去应对这些，

sentences.en: and for rising above some of like the terrible, frustrating things that workplace politics is going to throw at us.
sentences.zh: 并超越职场政治带给我们的那些糟糕、令人沮丧的事情。

sentences.en: So this is what we're discussing today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: It's going to be a big episode, but a very worthwhile, essential one.
sentences.zh: 这将是一期内容丰富、非常有价值且至关重要的节目。

sentences.en: If you are just beginning your career or in your 20s, without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 如果你刚开始职业生涯或正处于20多岁，废话不多说，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: A lot of the time, I think our early 20s and our 20s in general is like the first time we're really exposed to like very interesting and secretive workplace dynamics.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我认为我们20出头以及整个20多岁，是我们第一次真正接触到非常有趣且隐秘的职场动态。

sentences.en: I don't remember ever thinking about this before I started working.
sentences.zh: 我不记得在开始工作之前曾考虑过这些。

sentences.en: Yes, university, maybe high school had these like subtle hierarchies.
sentences.zh: 是的，大学，也许高中也有这些微妙的等级制度。

sentences.en: Same as like some of our early jobs, but only as you get older, do you realize how strange and like manipulative people can be and like the unwritten rules
sentences.zh: 和我们早期的一些工作一样，但只有当你年纪渐长，你才会意识到人们是多么奇怪和具有操纵性，以及职场中存在着那些不成文的规则，

sentences.en: that are at play in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 这些规则在起作用。

sentences.en: That is the office politics we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的办公室政治。

sentences.en: There is a literal whole, and I mean major, major discipline of psychology devoted to this very thing, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，心理学中确实有一个完整的、而且是非常重要的学科专门研究这个东西。

sentences.en: It's called organizational psychology.
sentences.zh: 它被称为组织心理学。

sentences.en: It essentially exclusively focuses on why people behave the way they do at work because we know work is such a huge part of our human lives and human identity.
sentences.zh: 它基本上专门研究人们为什么在工作中表现出那样的行为，因为我们知道工作是我们人类生活和人类身份中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It makes sense that it is as complicated as relationships, as complicated as marriages, as family.
sentences.zh: 它像人际关系、婚姻、家庭一样复杂，这也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: So back to the office.
sentences.zh: 回到办公室的话题。

sentences.en: If you want to understand the complexities of office politics, you first have to understand that every office has, or every workplace has two structures,
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解办公室政治的复杂性，你首先必须明白每个办公室或每个工作场所都有两种结构，

sentences.en: the formal hierarchy and the informal network.
sentences.zh: 正式的等级制度和非正式的网络。

sentences.en: So on paper, the hierarchy is very clear.
sentences.zh: 在纸面上，等级制度非常清晰。

sentences.en: You know, you have managers, directors, executives, interns, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有经理、总监、高管、实习生等等。

sentences.en: This is like bureaucratic authority, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像官僚权威，对吧？

sentences.en: The people at the top have legitimate rule-based power over people at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 处于顶层的人对底层的人拥有合法的、基于规则的权力。

sentences.en: You know, who has the title?
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁拥有头衔？

sentences.en: Who does the budgets?
sentences.zh: 谁负责预算？

sentences.en: Who does the performance reviews?
sentences.zh: 谁负责绩效评估？

sentences.en: Who is in charge?
sentences.zh: 谁说了算？

sentences.en: Alongside this though, is another structure that is more influential.
sentences.zh: 然而，与此同时，还有另一种结构更具影响力。

sentences.en: This is the informal network.
sentences.zh: 这就是非正式网络。

sentences.en: So these are the relationships.
sentences.zh: 这些就是人际关系。

sentences.en: These are the relationships that determine who gets consulted, who actually shapes the decisions, who is actually trusted with sensitive information.
sentences.zh: 正是这些关系决定了谁会被咨询，谁真正塑造了决策，谁真正被信任处理敏感信息。

sentences.en: And then also who makes more money, who gets the promotions, even if that power structure doesn't line up with the formal power structure.
sentences.zh: 还有谁赚更多的钱，谁得到晋升，即使这种权力结构与正式的权力结构并不一致。

sentences.en: This is sometimes what they call the shadow organization.
sentences.zh: 这有时被称为影子组织。

sentences.en: It's like these unspoken channels of influence that you have to be aware of if you want to play the game of work.
sentences.zh: 如果你想玩转职场游戏，就必须意识到这些不成文的影响力渠道。

sentences.en: There is this classic theory from the 50s
sentences.zh: 有一个来自50年代的经典理论，

sentences.en: about the five main sources of workplace power.
sentences.zh: 关于职场权力的五个主要来源。

sentences.en: And this is the other thing you have to be aware of if you want to navigate the complexities of office life.
sentences.zh: 如果你想驾驭办公室生活的复杂性，这是你必须意识到的另一件事。

sentences.en: If you want to have influence at work, you can have one of these five forms of power.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在工作中拥有影响力，你可以拥有这五种权力中的一种。

sentences.en: Legitimate power.
sentences.zh: 合法权力。

sentences.en: So the kind of power that is granted by authority.
sentences.zh: 即由权威授予的那种权力。

sentences.en: Reward power.
sentences.zh: 奖励权力。

sentences.en: Power in your ability to provide benefits, praise, recognition.
sentences.zh: 提供福利、赞美、认可的能力所带来的权力。

sentences.en: Coercive power.
sentences.zh: 强制权力。

sentences.en: The power to punish.
sentences.zh: 惩罚的权力。

sentences.en: Expert power.
sentences.zh: 专家权力。

sentences.en: The power of knowledge and competence.
sentences.zh: 知识和能力带来的权力。

sentences.en: And finally, reverent power.
sentences.zh: 最后，参照权力。

sentences.en: The ability to influence things through charisma and through likability.
sentences.zh: 通过个人魅力和讨人喜欢来影响事物的能力。

sentences.en: In your 20s, like you likely don't have much legitimate power yet.
sentences.zh: 在20多岁时，你可能还没有多少合法权力。

sentences.en: And I mean, if you do, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你有，那太棒了。

sentences.en: Like that's really cool.
sentences.zh: 那真的很酷。

sentences.en: If you are the CEO of something.
sentences.zh: 如果你是某家公司的CEO。

sentences.en: But most people in their 20s don't decide how much people get paid.
sentences.zh: 但大多数20多岁的人并不能决定别人的薪水。

sentences.en: You can't really fire or hire en masse.
sentences.zh: 你不能随意大规模解雇或招聘。

sentences.en: What you do have though is referent and expert power.
sentences.zh: 但你确实拥有参照权力和专家权力。

sentences.en: You can become indispensable by developing the knowledge and skills that other people don't have time for and they need to rely on you to do.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过发展别人没时间学习、且需要依赖你才能完成的知识和技能，让自己变得不可或缺。

sentences.en: You can also build alliances.
sentences.zh: 你也可以建立联盟。

sentences.en: You can collaborate with people.
sentences.zh: 你可以与人合作。

sentences.en: You can be nice to people.
sentences.zh: 你可以对人友善。

sentences.en: If you've ever heard the term personality hire, this is what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果你听说过“性格雇佣”这个词，这就是我们所说的。

sentences.en: People always dismiss the personality hire.
sentences.zh: 人们总是看不起“性格雇佣”。

sentences.en: But all that means is that you have great soft skills.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着你拥有出色的软技能。

sentences.en: You are enjoyable to be around.
sentences.zh: 你是一个让人相处愉快的人。

sentences.en: You're a morale booster.
sentences.zh: 你是士气提振者。

sentences.en: You are a fresh perspective.
sentences.zh: 你带来了新鲜的视角。

sentences.en: That is a huge asset in your 20s when a lot of people are very jaded.
sentences.zh: 在很多人都感到厌倦的20多岁，这是一个巨大的资产。

sentences.en: You have something others don't.
sentences.zh: 你拥有别人没有的东西。

sentences.en: You have to use whatever you can including that to your advantage.
sentences.zh: 你必须利用你能利用的一切，包括这一点，来为自己谋利。

sentences.en: You being a nice person to be around helps your boss.
sentences.zh: 你作为一个让人相处愉快的人，这有助于你的老板。

sentences.en: It strokes their ego.
sentences.zh: 这满足了他们的自尊心。

sentences.en: It makes them feel good.
sentences.zh: 这让他们感觉良好。

sentences.en: Which, yeah, may not be able to outperform somebody who is making three times as much as you.
sentences.zh: 虽然这可能无法胜过那些薪水是你三倍的人，

sentences.en: May not be able to outperform a very complex skill.
sentences.zh: 可能无法胜过非常复杂的专业技能，

sentences.en: But that small addition on top of the other things you're doing and the other skills you do have gives you great power.
sentences.zh: 但除了你正在做的其他事情和你拥有的其他技能之外，那一点点加成给了你巨大的力量。

sentences.en: You give something.
sentences.zh: 你付出了某些东西。

sentences.en: You are giving your personality.
sentences.zh: 你在贡献你的个性。

sentences.en: They are getting something in return from that.
sentences.zh: 他们从中得到了回报。

sentences.en: One of the most useful psychological frameworks for office politics is basically exactly this.
sentences.zh: 办公室政治中最有用的心理学框架之一基本上就是这个。

sentences.en: It's called social exchange theory.
sentences.zh: 它被称为社会交换理论。

sentences.en: It was first proposed by
sentences.zh: 它最初由George Homans在50年代提出，

sentences.en: George Homans like in the 50s.
sentences.zh: 我想在60年代得到了进一步发展。

sentences.en: I think it was further developed in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 你会听到社会交换理论被应用于从人际关系到工作，再到我们对待宠物的一切事物中。

sentences.en: You'll hear social exchange theory talked about in everything from relationships to work to our pets.
sentences.zh: 但它本质上认为，所有的人际关系，所有的一般关系，都基于交换原则。

sentences.en: But it essentially suggests that all human relationships, all relationships in general, operate on a principle of exchange.
sentences.zh: 我们给予并接收资源，无论是金钱等物质资源，还是爱与尊重等情感资源。

sentences.en: We give and we receive resources, whether that is material resources like money, emotional resources like love and respect.
sentences.zh: 当交换平衡时，关系就会蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: Relationships thrive when the exchange is balanced.
sentences.zh: 而当关系感到失衡时，它们就会受损。

sentences.en: And they suffer when they feel one-sided.
sentences.zh: 在办公室里，这种情况不断出现。

sentences.en: In an office, this shows up constantly.
sentences.zh: 这种交换理论实际上就是所有办公室政治的基础。

sentences.en: This exchange theory is literally the basis of all office politics.
sentences.zh: 你帮助同事赶上截止日期。

sentences.en: You help a co-worker meet a deadline.
sentences.zh: 他们后来会在晋升时为你说话。

sentences.en: They later advocate for you during like promotion time.
sentences.zh: 你分享功劳。

sentences.en: You share credit.
sentences.zh: 别人也与你分享功劳。

sentences.en: Others share credit with you.
sentences.zh: 你让你的老板感到时髦、年轻、酷且有趣。

sentences.en: You make your boss feel hip and young and cool and fun.
sentences.zh: 他们会成为一个好老板。

sentences.en: They're going to be a nice boss.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，

sentences.en: Back to you.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一些东西。

sentences.en: You're going to get stuff in return.
sentences.zh: 社会交换理论是平衡的。

sentences.en: The social exchange theory is balanced.
sentences.zh: 交换理论基本上是平衡的。

sentences.en: The exchange theory is balanced basically.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，它也解释了为什么办公室的氛围会变得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: On the flip side, it also explains why the energy of an office can become really toxic.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得——我认为这是我们年轻时都有过的经历——如果你觉得你在无休止地付出一切，你的忠诚、你的想法、

sentences.en: If you feel like, and I think this is an experience a lot of us have when we're younger, if you feel like you are endlessly giving everything, your loyalty, your ideas,
sentences.zh: 你的夜晚，而你没有得到任何认可、任何支持、任何金钱，那绝对是滋生怨恨的温床。

sentences.en: your evenings, and you are not receiving any recognition, any support, any money, that is a surefire way for resentment to build.
sentences.zh: 就像你会因为朋友或恋人从不回报你的计划，从不回报你在他们生日时投入的努力而感到非常沮丧一样，

sentences.en: Just like you would get super frustrated at a friend or a romantic partner for never reciprocating
sentences.zh: 这一切同样发生在工作中，只是现在对象是你的同事，而且可以说你可能见到他们的次数更多，并且你也不能像对待一个糟糕的朋友那样直接结束关系然后走开。

sentences.en: plans, never reciprocating the effort you put into their birthday.
sentences.zh: 他们和你一样都在那里。

sentences.en: This is all happening at work equally except now it's with your co-workers and you arguably probably see them a lot more and you also can't just end the relationship and walk away
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们不能在心理层面上忽视这些东西。

sentences.en: the way that you probably could do with a bad friend.
